== CYCLE CLOCKS — a public event-time instrument (3 November 2026) ==

'''CYCLE CLOCKS''' (''Цикловые часы'') is a Project BOG public mathematical and interactive software instrument. Concept: Bogdan Sergienko. Mathematical, software and editorial collaboration: CCAI KAI. The separate AI research tool Quark does not own or physically power the clock.

'''[https://bogsergienko.github.io/bog-sense-atlas/cycle-clocks/index.html OPEN THE INTERACTIVE CYCLE CLOCKS]'''

Source and reproducibility: [https://github.com/BogSergienko/bog-sense-atlas/tree/main/cycle-clocks Cycle Clocks source and instructions].

=== The cyclic address ===
The model uses two labelled event types, A and B, their joint event, and reversible state <math>X=(a,b,h)\in\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_q\times\mathbb{Z}_2</math>. Its visible projection <math>\pi(X)=(a,b)</math> need not encode the complete state. At <math>q=3</math>, the joint events give a visible six-event recurrence but a complete twelve-event recurrence; <math>q=4</math> supplies a negative control. The event order A→B vs B→A can matter at selected boundaries.

The counter is an event address, not a replacement physical second. This tool is a finite reversible mathematical prototype, not a verified new physical law, atomic clock or astronomical finding.

=== Human and AI research entrance ===
'''OPEN:''' Run the clock, compare independent orders, check the 6/12 case and its null control.
'''RETURN:''' Record the initial state, q, labelled event sequence, observed return and a counterexample or new application.
'''CLOSE:''' Disagreement and free exit are welcome; results should keep their sources.
